standard: Limited obvious-error screen only, not exhaustive historical authentication or approval of every claim. Preserve known historical alternatives; do not reject uncertain claims merely for lacking absolute proof.

rows.title: Abiathar
rows.reason: Adonijah's attempted takeover and Abiathar's support occurred before David died, not after.

rows.title: Ahaz
rows.reason: Conflates Israel's Assyrian deportation with Judah's later Babylonian exile.

rows.title: Amalek, Amalekite
rows.reason: Claims hostility began only once Israel entered Canaan, but the Amalekites fought Israel at Rephidim during the Exodus.

rows.title: Ammon, Ammonite
rows.reason: Attributes hiring Balaam to the Ammonites; Balak of Moab sent for him.

rows.title: Antioch
rows.reason: Conflates persecution at Pisidian Antioch with the stoning of Paul at Lystra by visitors FROM Antioch and Iconium.

rows.title: Aram, Aramean, Aramaic, Aram of Damascus
Balaam
rows.reason: Calls Balak a Midianite king; the text explicitly identifies him as king of Moab.

rows.title: Bethany
rows.reason: Cites John 1:28's Bethany beyond the Jordan for the different Bethany near Jerusalem, home of Lazarus.

rows.title: Beth Shemesh
rows.reason: Claims Philistines were bringing the ark back to Jerusalem; the actual route was Beth-shemesh then Kiriath-jearim.

rows.title: Cain
rows.reason: Places Cain's protective mark specifically on his forehead although Genesis never specifies its location.

rows.title: Cilicia
rows.reason: Places Cilicia on the Aegean coast instead of the Mediterranean coast.

rows.title: Corinth, Corinthians
rows.reason: Calls Paul's 18-month Corinth stay his first missionary journey instead of his second.

rows.title: Hamath, Hamathites, Lebo Hamath, Hamath Rabbah
Herod, Herod Antipas
rows.reason: Calls Agrippa I Antipas's son; Agrippa I was his nephew (Aristobulus IV's son).

rows.title: Jehoiachin
rows.reason: Calls Manasseh Jehoiachin's grandfather; several generations intervene: Manasseh, Amon, Josiah, Jehoiakim, Jehoiachin.

rows.title: Jehoram, Joram
rows.reason: Places ninth-century King Jehoram alongside Jeremiah, Daniel and Ezekiel, who belong centuries later.

rows.title: Jezreel, Jezreelite
rows.reason: Places Jezreel southwest of the Dead/Salt Sea instead of in northern Israel's Jezreel Valley.

rows.title: Nehemiah
rows.reason: Claims Nehemiah was personally deported by Babylonians, an unattested life event inconsistent with the later Persian-period setting.

rows.title: Nile River, River of Egypt, the Nile
Obadiah
rows.reason: States Jeremiah, Daniel and Ezekiel prophesied during a proposed ninth-century Obadiah dating; those periods do not overlap.

rows.title: Omri
rows.reason: Says Omri ruled all twelve years in Tirzah; Scripture says only six years there, followed by Samaria.

rows.title: Paddan Aram
rows.reason: Calls Rebekah Bethuel's granddaughter rather than his daughter and Nahor's granddaughter.

rows.title: Peor, Mount Peor, Baal Peor
rows.reason: States Beth-peor is where Moses died; the death scene is Mount Nebo/Pisgah, with burial opposite Beth-peor.

rows.title: Priscilla, Prisca
rows.reason: Says Emperor Claudius expelled Christians from Rome; Acts says he ordered Jews to leave.

rows.title: Ramah
rows.reason: Claims Rachel died at Ramah; Genesis locates her death and burial by the road to Ephrath/Bethlehem.

rows.title: Rapha, Raphaites, the Valley of the Raphaites
Sea of Galilee, Sea of Kinnereth, lake of Gennesaret, Sea of Tiberias
Seir, sons of Seir, Mount Seir, mountains of Seir, land of Seir
the sea, the Great Sea, the western sea
Tirzah
rows.reason: Identifies Tirzah as Gilead's daughter/Manasseh's granddaughter; she is Zelophehad's daughter, several generations later.
